title: Controlling Electron-Beam-Induced Charging in Colloidal Quantum Dots
authors: Sven Ebel, Alina Myslovska, Stefano Vezzoli, Iwan Moreels, Sergii Morozov
abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are attractive nanoscale emitters, yet their cathodoluminescence (CL) response remains poorly understood and often unstable under electron-beam excitation, limiting CL spectroscopy and electron-beam-based device processing. Here, we investigate the CL mechanism and strategies to improve its stability using highly photostable, structurally homogeneous giant-shell CdSe/CdS QDs combined with in situ CL and photoluminescence (PL) measurements. By identifying distinct signatures of excited states in both lifetime and spectral measurements, we demonstrate that the CL response is governed by electron-beam-induced charging. Charge accumulation drives multiexciton generation even at relatively low currents, leading to a pronounced blueshift, shorter average lifetimes, and rapid cathodobleaching. To test this further, we employ indirect excitation to reach sub-pA currents beyond the limits of typical electron beams, showing that neutral-exciton emission can be partially recovered and cathodobleaching mitigated, although charging cannot be fully suppressed. Furthermore, by replacing long insulating ligands with shorter ones, we improve charge drainage and strongly suppress biexciton formation. Together, these results show that biexciton formation can be controlled by limiting charge accumulation, providing a practical route toward stable CL for spectroscopy, imaging, and electron-beam-compatible photonic devices.
summary: The research investigates why colloidal quantum dots exhibit unstable cathodoluminescence under electron beams. They demonstrate that this instability stems from detrimental electron-beam-induced charging, which drives multiexciton formation. By replacing long surface ligands with shorter ones, the researchers successfully improve charge drainage and stabilize the emission process for practical device applications.
main_problem: The primary challenge is understanding and stabilizing the unstable Cathodoluminescence (CL) response of Colloidal Quantum Dots (QDs) when excited by an electron beam.
main_result: The CL instability, blueshift, and bleaching are shown to be governed by electron-beam-induced charging, which can be mitigated by using shorter surface ligands to improve charge drainage.
method: In situ measurements combining Cathodoluminescence (CL) and Photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, alongside ligand exchange experiments, were used to probe excited state dynamics.
model_or_system: The system involves giant-shell CdSe/CdS colloidal quantum dots. The analysis distinguishes between neutral excitons ($	ext{X}_0$), charged excitons ($	ext{X}^*$), and biexcitons ($	ext{XX}$) using spectral fitting.
key_observables: Spectral evolution (blueshift), decay lifetimes, relative contributions of $	ext{X}^0$, $	ext{X}^*$, and $	ext{XX}$ components, and intensity degradation (cathodobleaching).
important_parameters: Electron beam current (from high to sub-pA regimes), ligand length (long oleate vs. short MPA), and excitation voltage.
main_assumptions: The study assumes that charge accumulation is the central mechanism driving the observed instability in the CL response, rather than solely local heating or surface modification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate setup schematics, TEM images of QDs, spectral evolution (blueshift) and intensity degradation under electron beam exposure, and comparisons between PL/CL spectra before and after ligand treatment.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the instability problem using CL/PL measurements, identifying charge accumulation as the cause via current dependence studies, and finally proposing a solution through surface chemistry modification (ligand exchange) to control multi-exciton formation.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental demonstration of controlling many-body dynamics (biexciton generation) in nanoscale emitters by manipulating the charge environment, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and charge transport in solid-state nanodevices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Experimental setup for in situ CL and PL of QDs. (a) SEM-based CL setup with a parabolic mirror for light collection. QDs are excited by the electron beam to generate CL, which is analyzed using a spectrometer and a Hanbury Brown– Twiss (HBT) interferometer with two avalanche photodiodes (APDs) connected to a time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC) module. A laser is coupled into the same optical path via a dichroic mirror (DM) to excite PL at the focal point of the parabolic mirror. (b) TEM image of giant-shell QDs (scale bar: 25 nm). (c) Lifetime measurements under electron-beam (CL) and laser (PL) excitation. (d-e) Intensity time traces of QDs under laser and electron beam...

FIG. 2: Biexciton contribution in CL. (a) PL spec- trum decomposed into neutral exciton (X0), charged exciton (X∗), and biexciton (XX) contributions with corresponding cumulative fit. (b) CL spectrum decomposed into the same components, showing enhanced biexciton emission (magenta). (c) Relative biexciton contribution as a function of beam cur- rent for 5 keV and 30 keV excitation.

FIG. 3: CL response at ultra-low currents. (a) Schematic of direct (purple) and indirect (gray) excitation of QDs. (b) SEM image of a QD cluster indicating beam po- sitions for direct (purple) and indirect excitation 5 µm away from the cluster (gray). (c) Emission spectra under direct and indirect (5 µm) excitation compared to PL. (d) Decay histograms in PL (blue), direct (purple) and indirect (grey, at 5 µm) CL. (e) Normalized intensity time trace under direct excitation at 6 pA showing bleaching, and under sub-pA indi- rect excitation at 9 µm showing stable emission.

FIG. 4: Effect of ligand exchange on biexciton generation. (a) Schematic of ligand exchange from long oleate ligands (brown) to short MPA ligands (green). (b,c) PL spectra and decay histograms before and after ligand exchange. (d) High- current CL spectra, demonstrating suppression of the biexciton emission after replacing long oleate ligands with shorter MPA ligands. Both spectra are normalized at 660 nm to highlight the contribution of biexciton emission. (e) Low-current CL decay histograms before and after ligand exchange, together with three-exponential fits (red). (f) Relative biexciton contribution after ligand exchange over a wide range of electron-beam currents for 5 keV and 30 keV.
